correctness.rationale: Reconstructed graph from modular edges u_i-u_{i+1},u_i-v_i,v_i-v_{i+3}; graph has 20 vertices/30 edges. All shortest-path tables and distance <=2 cliques yield (20,90,120,30) simplicial face vector and zero five-cliques. Independently performed 30 legitimate free triangle-tetrahedron elementary collapses leaving a 2-complex with (20,90,90) faces. For its 1-skeleton, 19 spanning-tree edges give 71 non-tree generators; 90 triangle relators (nontrivial reduced relators as presented) admit 71 exact generator-once Tietze eliminations with complete substitutions leaving no relators/generators. Hence pi1 trivial, not merely abelianization. Euler characteristic 20 implies H2=Z^19, and Hurewicz plus homology Whitehead theorem gives wedge of nineteen S2. All finite computations reconstructed from graph equations rather than saved output.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is a canonical cubic girth-six incidence/generalized Petersen graph and scale two is a natural first thickening at the girth boundary. An explicit integral homotopy type with a nonabelian pi1 certificate (19 spheres) is a meaningful exact benchmark for graph-metric Rips theory, distinct from previously studied Desargues Cech complexes and GP(n,2) powers.

final_claim: For the Desargues graph GP(10,3) with unit-edge intrinsic shortest-path metric, the inclusive scale-two Vietoris-Rips complex is homotopy equivalent over integers to a wedge of 19 two-spheres.
limitations: Intrinsic shortest-path metric, inclusive threshold exactly 2, GP(10,3) only; no persistence or equivariant splitting.
